messages.author: 9e8f9b870a2e6cdf
messages.subject: scale_x_datetime: bug report and patch
parts:
Hoi,

I think there is a bug in the handling of the tz parameter of scale_x_datetime().  When major = 'day' this bug causes the major breaks not to be on day boundaries.

The cause of this bug is that not all methods that compute the labels and breaks take in account the specified timezone.

Below is an example that demonstrates this bug.

require(ggplot2)
start_date <- ISOdate( 2001, 12, 1, 0, 0, tz = "EST" )
timestamps <- start_date + seq( 0, 48*3600, by = 3600 )

testframe <- data.frame(
    tms  = timestamps,
    hour =  as.POSIXlt( timestamps )$hour
)

p <- ggplot( testframe, aes( x=tms, y=hour ) ) + geom_point() + geom_line()
plot1 <- p + scale_x_datetime(
           major = 'day',
           minor = '1 hour',
           tz="EST"
         )

This code create a dataframe with 48 timestamps. 
Timestamps that start at 01 Dec 2001 00:00, incremented by 1 hour, and ends at 03 Dec 2001 00:00.
They are defined in the timezone EST, which is different from my timezone CET.

The dataframe also contains for each timestamp the hour component of each timestamp.  We plot the hour component as function of the timestamp with major breaks on the day boundary.

The resulting plot, plot1, is attached.


I have presumed the parameter tz to mean -- compute the labels and breaks in the specified timezone.
Since the specified timezone and the timezone of the dataset are equal I expected the following:
- the plot that starts at 01 Dec 2001 00:00
- the plot ends at 03 Dec 2001 00:00. 
- The major breaks are at 01, 02, and 03 Dec (00:00 hours)
- A sawtooth wave that starts at 0 at the each major break.

The plot starts however well before 01 Dec and the sawtooth wave does not start at 0 at the major breaks.

Note that my own timezone is 'CET', and that the problem only occurs when the timezone used for the data is different from
my own timezone.  (If you happen to be living in a EST , change EST in the code to GMT to reproduce the bug.)


The following plot shows the reason (attached as plot2.png)

plot2 <- p + scale_x_datetime(
           major = 'day',
           minor = '1 hour',
           format="%d/%b %H:%M %Z",
           tz="EST"
        )

The major breaks are not on the day boundaries, but at 18:00 hours.

The problem is, I think, in scale-datetime.r in the methods input_breaks() and output_breaks().  After converting the
result of input_set() to time format with to_time().  The tz attribute is not set, and in further computations the tz of the system is used.


The following patch solves this problem.

https://github.com/gumpu/ggplot2/commit/ee1487df47d89d8c69c88ff73d2a2fd512de6c50

The attached plot plot1_fixed.png shows the result of the patch.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: scale_x_datetime: bug report and patch
parts:
Hi:

I think this is related to the repeated date issue reported by Sarah McKinnon in another thread. When I looked at her data briefly, I extracted the date part and converted it with as.Date(). Comparing the new dates with the old (which contained H:M:S + ...) information, I noticed there was a 7-hour offset between the correct day in her original data and the day reported with the created variable (the number of hours may be due to a time zone difference - mine is PST [US]).

HTH,
Dennis

Hi Dennis,

Looks like it.  I was able to reproduce the bug from that thread by selecting the EST timezone.  In addition there is a daylight saving time change in the given period.
Given the mix of timezone this might confuse fullseq_date() in date-time.r

Have fun,
Frans.
